primaryQuery: Home Assistant bathroom fan humidity automation
readerQuestion: How do I make Home Assistant turn a bathroom fan on when a shower raises the humidity, then turn it off after the room has dried, without seasonal false starts or broken manual control?
selectedBecause: The same start-on-shower and stop-when-dry problem recurs across current r/homeassistant and Home Assistant Community discussions, including a long-running blueprint thread with 2026 activity. Exact-query results offer isolated blueprints, fixed-threshold examples, and individual project notes, but no leading homeowner guide clearly compares a fixed target with a rate-of-rise or room-baseline approach, protects manual operation, and adds a maximum-runtime fallback. Home Assistant's current Statistics, Derivative, Trend, Generic Hygrostat, and humidity-trigger documentation now provide solid primary evidence for those choices. The question is durable, practical, safe to answer without electrical wiring instructions, strongly aligned with reliable local automation, and absent from Tara's 133 existing article URLs. Current Search Console opportunities already map their high-impression queries to other owner paths and contain no close variation of this question.

demandSignals.evidence: The exact search returns community blueprints, project logs, a simple fixed-threshold example, and vendor-neutral snippets, but no leading result gives a plain decision between fixed humidity, shower-relative rise, and dry-room settling while also preserving manual control and failure behavior.

A current discussion asks where a bathroom humidity sensor should go and how to make shower detection reliable, showing that sensor placement and useful control remain active homeowner problems rather than a solved historical curiosity.

A separate current discussion shares a rate-of-change bathroom-fan automation and draws follow-up questions about tuning, demonstrating continuing interest in a shower-relative approach instead of one fixed humidity number.
The long-running bathroom-fan blueprint discussion remains active in 2026 and repeatedly covers humidity rise, falling trends, minimum and maximum runtime, manual operation, and back-to-back showers.
An independent question asks how to start a fan after a percentage rise within a time window rather than at one absolute number, capturing the central seasonal false-trigger problem.

A maintained community blueprint implements the recurring need with rising and falling humidity logic, timing controls, and safeguards, providing additional independent evidence that the full problem extends beyond a one-line threshold.

searchReview.query: Home Assistant bathroom fan humidity automation
searchReview.intent: The searcher wants a reliable Home Assistant setup that recognizes a shower, starts an exhaust fan promptly, stops only after the bathroom has dried, leaves the wall control useful, and does not behave badly as normal humidity changes with the season.
searchReview.resultGap: Current results are fragmented. Home Assistant's direct example shows a fixed threshold, while community blueprints and project pages use more resilient rise-rate or baseline logic without first explaining which method a non-technical homeowner should choose. Leading results rarely put sensor placement, manual operation, minimum and maximum runtime, back-to-back showers, stale sensors, Home Assistant downtime, and fan-rated electrical controls into one clear plan.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant Statistics integration
officialSources.supports: Statistics helpers can track a rolling humidity baseline and the documentation specifically describes detecting when bathroom humidity settles after a hot shower; helper state is restored after restart.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant Derivative integration
officialSources.supports: The Derivative helper measures rate of change and supports a time window that smooths noisy sensor readings.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant Trend integration
officialSources.supports: A Trend helper can classify a numeric sensor as rising or falling after it has received enough samples.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant Generic Hygrostat integration
officialSources.supports: Generic Hygrostat provides fixed-target humidity control with tolerances, minimum cycle durations, and stale-sensor safety behavior for a switch-controlled fan or humidifier.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant humidity crossed-threshold trigger documentation
officialSources.supports: The current automation editor can trigger once when humidity crosses a chosen threshold, can require the reading to remain there for a duration, and includes a direct bathroom-fan example.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant Timer integration
officialSources.supports: A Timer helper can keep a bathroom fan running for a chosen period, and starting an active timer restarts its countdown for a later shower.

officialSources.name: US EPA mold and moisture guidance
officialSources.supports: Indoor relative humidity should generally stay below 60 percent, ideally around 30 to 50 percent, while moisture sources and water problems still require correction.

officialSources.name: Panasonic WhisperSense bathroom fan documentation
officialSources.supports: A purpose-built fan with built-in humidity sensing is a current standalone alternative that can control ventilation without depending on Home Assistant.

existingCoverage.decision: No current Tara page owns humidity-based bathroom-fan control. The manual-override article owns the general rule for preserving physical controls, the troubleshooting article owns traces and failed automations, the outage article owns broader controller-failure behavior, and /home-automation-kit/ owns the commercial local-routines intent. The new page will answer only the bathroom ventilation setup decision, link to those established pages descriptively, and keep its one commercial recommendation on /home-automation-kit/.
